You want import threading.csv to Python, plot "threads" and "data" columns as linear regression up to 1000, test size 10%? I show you how. 

First, import necessary libraries. 
```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
```

Next, import data. 
```python
df = pd.read_csv('threading.csv')
```

Then, split data into training and testing sets. 
```python
X = df['threads'].values.reshape(-1, 1)
y = df['data'].values.reshape(-1, 1)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.1, random_state=42)
```

Now, fit linear regression model. 
```python
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
```

Next, make predictions. 
```python
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
```

Then, calculate mean squared error. 
```python
mse = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred)
print('Mean Squared Error:', mse)
```

Finally, plot results. 
```python
plt.scatter(X_test, y_test, color='blue', label='Actual')
plt.plot(X_test, y_pred, color='red', label='Predicted')
plt.xlabel('Threads')
plt.ylabel('Data')
plt.title('Linear Regression')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```
